edges.description: IFN-gamma increases NOD2 abundance and permits ligand-independent inflammatory signaling in disease-specific macrophage models.
intermediate_mechanisms: IFN-gamma-dependent NOD2 upregulation in mutant macrophages

edges.description: A second mechanistic model links Blau variants to reduced canonical NOD2-RIPK2 signaling and loss of IRF4-mediated restraint on parallel innate responses.
IFN-gamma-primed mutant NOD2 drives abnormal inflammatory cytokine production.
Loss of IRF4-mediated restraint permits exaggerated cytokine responses to concurrent innate signals.
intermediate_mechanisms: Reduced IRF4 induction and failed suppression of TLR signaling

edges.description: Sustained dysregulated innate inflammation is modeled upstream of tissue granuloma formation.
Granulomatous synovitis causes progressive polyarthritis.
Granulomatous uveitis threatens vision.
Non-caseating granulomas form in the dermis.
Granulomatous inflammation extends to visceral organs and the vasculature.
Systemic granulomatous autoinflammation can include recurrent fever.
Granulomatous synovitis manifests clinically as polyarticular arthritis.
Chronic granulomatous tenosynovitis and joint involvement can present with camptodactyly.
intermediate_mechanisms: Chronic tenosynovitis and joint contracture limit finger extension.

edges.description: Dysplastic bone changes are associated with the characteristic arthropathy, although the causal route from NOD2 signaling to bone morphology is unknown.
Ocular granulomatous inflammation manifests as uveitis/panuveitis.
Chronic uveitis and its complications produce visual impairment.
Cataract is a complication of chronic ocular inflammation.
Chronic uveitis and its treatment can be complicated by glaucoma.
Dermal granulomas manifest as the characteristic rash or dermatitis.
Expanded vascular involvement manifests as vasculitis.
Expanded visceral involvement can include interstitial lung disease.

nodes.description: Monoclonal TNF inhibitors such as adalimumab or infliximab are used for persistent uveitis or arthritis. Cohorts show frequent initial responses, but relapse and secondary loss of efficacy are common, and comparative evidence remains insufficient.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features, treatment strategies, and long-term outcomes of Blau syndrome: a 10-year experience from a Chinese cohort.
evidence.snippet: While 6 (46.2%) patients achieved sustained stability, relapse or secondary loss of efficacy occurred in 6 (46.2%) patients, necessitating treatment adjustments.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of uveitis in Blau syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: The proportion of children showing improvement of uveitis was 20 % (95 % CI 2-46) and 22 % (95 % CI3-47) for cDMARDs and bDMARDs respectively (χ20.23, p = 0.631).

nodes.description: Dysplastic bony changes on radiographs, a previously unrecognized feature found in two-thirds of patients in the multicentre study. May suggest a role for NOD2 in bone morphogenesis and could have diagnostic value.

evidence.reference_title: Blau syndrome: cross-sectional data from a multicentre study of clinical, radiological and functional outcomes.

nodes.description: Flexion contractures of fingers due to chronic granulomatous tenosynovitis, a characteristic feature of Blau syndrome joint involvement.

evidence.reference_title: Blau Syndrome: Challenging Molecular Genetic Diagnostics of Autoinflammatory Disease.

nodes.description: Blau-associated NOD2 variants can reduce MDP-responsive RIPK2 signaling and IRF4 induction, weakening NOD2-mediated suppression of concurrent TLR responses. This model differs from simple constitutive activation.

nodes.description: Context-dependent mutant-NOD2 signaling and defective innate cross-regulation converge on abnormal macrophage cytokine production. The precise cytokine hierarchy in human lesions remains incompletely defined.

nodes.description: Tofacitinib suppresses IFN-gamma-induced NOD2 expression in cell models and has retrospective clinical evidence in refractory Blau syndrome. It remains an emerging option under prospective evaluation rather than an established standard.
